objective: Prove: for every doubly periodic board (a Z^2-periodic map with rings at vertices and contacts at edges, ring cells as in the program's networks, any g), the route reading between cells is, up to an additive constant, the gauge of the convex polygon spanned by displacement over length of the simple cycles of the finite quotient of its route digraph; the same holds for the board's ring graph; so no periodic board's reading is round.
title: On every periodic board the route reading is a polygon norm up to a constant
